air_horn.notes: The canned air horn with the red plastic trumpet. Banned at the gate, smuggled in a sock.

amp_kit.notes: The amp wiring kit: a coil of fat red power wire, a short blue ground, an inline fuse holder you could see the fuse through, and a ring terminal crimped with pliers.

asian_pear.notes: A Korean pear the size of a softball, golden-brown and freckled, in its white foam net sock.

audio_stickers.notes: The window decals: a long windshield banner in chrome die-cut letters, plus the stickers that came in every box, so the whole lot knew what was in your trunk before they heard it.

av_cable.notes: Red, white, yellow: the three plugs, the split, the flat multi-out on the other end.

backpack.notes: One-strap-only backpack: suede bottom, front pocket, a pile of zipper pulls, iron-on patches, pins.

ball_mouse.notes: The two-button ball mouse, its retaining ring twisted off and the grey rubber ball rolled away from it, the way it went every time it stopped tracking. Rollers wore a gasket of gunk.

banana_milk.notes: The squat pale-yellow jug of banana milk with the foil peel top. Bought at every bathhouse and rest stop.

bass_knob.notes: The remote bass knob, screwed under the dash by your knee: one fat knob, BASS in white letters, a red light, and a cable running all the way back to the trunk. Turned it to the right. Always.

battle_top.notes: The battle top: a sharp tip, a heavy disc, a jagged attack ring, a printed chip on top.

beaded_curtain.notes: A tangle of strands torn off a beaded curtain: clear and colored plastic beads on string.

bean_bag_chunk.notes: A torn corner of a bean bag chair: vinyl or corduroy, the zipper, foam beads spilling out.

beanie_display_case.notes: The clear acrylic case: the bear never touched air again.

beanie_tag_protector.notes: Loose clear tag protectors, some still holding a heart tag snipped off something 'worthless'.

beanie_teeny.notes: The fast-food mini, still sealed in its baggie with the insert, because opening it kills the value.

beige_keyboard.notes: The whole beige keyboard: grey modifier keys, a numpad, three green lights, a coiled cord, and enough crumbs under the keys to feed a family through Y2K.

beige_tower.notes: The beige tower: two drive bays, a floppy slot, a TURBO button nobody understood and a red LED display bragging about megahertz.

big_x_console.notes: The huge black box with the crossed channel on top and the green glowing jewel.

bkr_sticker.notes: A BE KIND PLEASE REWIND sticker still stuck to a shard of black tape shell, the arrow pointing the way you never turned it.

black_cat.notes: A sitting cat figurine: tall, slim, ears up, tail wrapped around the front.

blacklight.notes: An 18-inch blacklight tube in its black plastic fixture, the tube glowing purple.

blow_up_gloves.notes: Inflatable boxing gloves. Every punch made the same squeak.

bobblehead.notes: Stadium giveaway bobblehead: tiny body, enormous head on a spring, a face only a promo budget could love.

bubble_tape.notes: The tape-measure case of shredded gum, pulled out across the desk to measure everything but the gum.

bug_oven.notes: The bug-maker: a hot little oven, a metal mold full of bug-shaped dents, goop, and rubber bugs.

bunny_charm.notes: Our rabbit (the same one on the magazine covers), as a glossy black keepsake: round head, two tall ears leaning apart, one eye, a bow tie. Nobody's logo; everybody's bunny.

calpis_bottle.notes: The milky soft-drink bottle, white with blue polka dots. Tastes like a yogurt that went to heaven.

candy_scoop.notes: The scoop off the sweet wall, chained to nothing, in the bag by mistake.

car_amp.notes: The amp: an aluminum slab with fins like a radiator, an airbrushed top, a terminal block for the fat power wire and a row of lights that meant the alternator was crying.

car_rewinder.notes: The VHS rewinder shaped like a red sports car: pop the hood, drop the tape in, and it screamed through a two-hour movie in ninety seconds, then ejected the hood like a crash test.

card_binder_sheet.notes: A 9-pocket binder page of commons, sorted by team, one empty slot where the good card used to be.

card_toploader.notes: A rookie card in a rigid top-loader, penny-sleeved, because it was going to pay for college.

cassette_adapter.notes: The cassette adapter: a tape with no tape in it, a fake head where the tape should be, and a thin cord out the side to the portable CD player sliding around the passenger seat. Clicked forever.

cd_changer.notes: The trunk-mounted CD changer: a steel box bolted to the trunk floor, a sliding door, and a magazine of ten discs you loaded once in 1998 and never changed again.

cdr_sharpie.notes: A gold CD-R, Sharpie on the label side, burned at 4x after three coasters. Do not lend.

cdr_spindle.notes: The cake box of blank discs: black base, a post up the middle, a stack of shiny CD-Rs and a smoky clear dome that never screwed back on straight.

charm_phone.notes: A clamshell phone with more charm than phone: rhinestones on the lid, straps by the fistful.

chew_bar.notes: The fizzy chew bar: pink and blue wrapper, sherbet bits in the chew, two pence.

chews_trophy.notes: The orange goblet trophy from the kids' choice-ish awards, dripping slime off the rim on purpose.

chip_bag_3d.notes: The 1998 puffed-up 3D chips: a pillow bag of air and, somewhere, nine chips.

choc_bunny.notes: A hollow chocolate rabbit, ears bitten off first, in foil.

choc_egg_shell.notes: Broken shards of the egg: brown outside, white inside.

choco_pie_box.notes: The red box of marshmallow chocolate cakes, or one cake in its red wrapper, or one cake with a bite out.

chocolate_box.notes: The heart-shaped box: red foil lid, a few chocolates left in their brown cups.

clay_gem.notes: The purple gem from the shelf: a hand-cut clay diamond, flat top, a crown of facets, a point below.

clay_steak.notes: From the butcher shop: a clay cut of meat with a fat rim and a bone.

clip_player.notes: BIT CLIPZ: a music player the size of a cracker that plays one minute of one song, off a chip the size of a stamp. On a keychain clip, with spare song chips rattling around.

cola_bottles.notes: Gummy cola bottles: brown at the bottom, clear at the top, sometimes rolled in fizzy sugar.

cold_wallet.notes: A hardware wallet at a size you can read from across a room. The screen keeps its own material, so it still says SEED? from inside the ice.

console_16bit.notes: The black 16-bit slab: the big round well in the middle and the lettering stamped into it.

console_64.notes: The 64-bit grey slab: a raised spine with a cart slot, two sliders, four ports on the nose.

console_box.notes: The retail box: brand across the top, the console on the front, starbursts everywhere.

costume_mask.notes: A cheap drugstore vacuum-formed mask, the kind with the staple and the elastic that snapped.

cow_box.notes: The computer box with cow spots: black-and-white holstein cardboard, flaps open, the most exciting box that ever came to the house.

crackberry.notes: The email phone: a keyboard of forty tiny chiclets, a scroll wheel on the side, a red light blinking at dinner. Thumbs never recovered.

cranberry_log.notes: Canned cranberry sauce, still holding the can's rings.

crayon_box.notes: The 64-box: stadium seating for crayons, the sharpener in the back, half the points already gone.

crystal_cola.notes: The clear cola of 1993. Tasted like a cola that had seen a ghost.

cube_console.notes: The purple lunchbox: a cube, a round lid, a carry handle off the back.

dare_flag.notes: The obstacle-course flag you had to grab before the clock ran out. Slime drip on the pole: authentic.

disc_console.notes: The grey disc box: a round lid on the left, three round buttons on the right.

dream_catcher.notes: A mall dream catcher: suede-wrapped hoop, a web, plastic beads, three dangling feathers.

drink_pouch.notes: The foil drink pouch, straw stabbed through the dot on the third try.

dropbox_door.notes: A piece of the after-hours return slot, pried off the wall: painted steel, a flap that swung in, MOVIE RETURNS in vinyl letters, and one hundred thousand tapes shoved through it at 11:58 PM.

dual_screen_handheld.notes: The silver clamshell, open, two screens, a stylus parked in the back.

duel_card.notes: A duel-monstahs card: stars, ATK/DEF, and the brown spiral back everyone knows from across a cafeteria.

dvd_case.notes: The early-DVD keep case: black plastic, a clear sleeve over the cover, WIDESCREEN in a box, and a BLOCKBUSTED sticker over the actors' faces.

extension_cable.notes: The controller extension cable: a coiled mess and two chunky ends, so you could sit on the couch.

eye_pod.notes: The white one. Mirror-chrome back, a wheel you rubbed with your thumb, and the white earbuds that told the whole bus what you had.

faceplate_case.notes: The faceplate's hard case: a little clamshell the size of a glasses case, so nobody smashed your window for a deck with no face. They smashed it anyway.

famicom_cart.notes: The short, wide Japanese cartridge in a candy color, grip ridges on the sides, label on the front.

finger_skateboard.notes: A finger board: kicked nose and tail, tiny trucks, a real printed graphic underneath.

firework.notes: A cardboard tube with a fuse, label and all; some already went off.

fizzy_laces.notes: Sour laces in sugar, tangled the way they came out of the jar.

flag_bunting.notes: A string of little paper flags of every country in the group, off the front of the corner shop.

flick_figure.notes: The table-football man: a painted little player glued to a disc on a weighted half-ball. Flick to kick.

flop_it.notes: FLOP. TWIST. PULL. The arc-shaped command toy: bop cap in the middle, twist knob one end, pull handle the other.

flying_saucers.notes: Rice-paper flying saucers full of sherbet. The paper stuck to the roof of your mouth.

foam_bead_tub.notes: The tub of foam-bead clay, a sticky crunchy mound of it out on the table, the rest in the carpet forever.

foam_finger.notes: The giant foam #1 hand. Bought in the third inning, lost in the parking lot.

foam_football.notes: The soft indoor ball, the only kind allowed in the house. Still broke the lamp.

foam_shrimps.notes: Pink-and-white foam shrimps: curled, chalky, and nothing like a shrimp.

football_sticker.notes: One loose sticker, maybe a double, maybe the one you needed.

fried_eggs.notes: Gummy fried eggs: a white foam puddle and a yellow gummy yolk.

frosting_dip.notes: Cookies plus a well of frosting with sprinkles, foil lid peeled back. Everyone traded up for these.

fruit_chew.notes: The soft fruit chew in its stick pack, or a few loose pieces in their little wrappers.

fruit_computer.notes: The translucent all-in-one: candy-colored see-through back with the tube showing inside, a handle on top, a hockey-puck mouse somewhere. Came in five fruits. Nobody bought a printer that matched.

fruit_strip.notes: Three feet of rolled fruit leather, half unrolled, paper backing printed with jokes nobody laughed at.

fuzzy_poster.notes: A flocked velvet blacklight poster, curling off the wall, thumbtack holes in the corners.

gacha_capsule.notes: A capsule: clear top, colored bottom, a toy folded inside a paper slip.

gacha_figure.notes: A 200-yen figure: a tiny robot, a lazy cat or a pocket dinosaur. Painted, slightly off-register.

gacha_knob.notes: The front plate off a capsule machine: the coin slot and the crank you turned until it clicked.

game_case.notes: A black disc case with the sleeve art, and the disc half slid out of it.

gb_pocket.notes: The slimmed-down 1996 handheld: two AAA batteries, a black-and-white screen you could finally read.

gel_pens.notes: A fistful of glitter gel pens: clear barrels, sparkly ink tubes, see-through caps, the good ones.

giant_controller.notes: The brick: the biggest controller ever made, jewel in the middle, six face buttons.

gift_oil_bottle.notes: The bottle of cooking oil every Korean gift set came with, wedged between the cans.

glass_soda.notes: The tall glass bottle of fruit soda, mandarin or tamarind or lime, with the paper-look label.

glow_stars.notes: A handful of glow-in-the-dark ceiling stars and a crescent moon, sticky putty still on the backs.

gremlin.notes: The late-90s fuzzy owl-gremlin that talked all night. Original face, era-true colorways.

gremlin_batteries.notes: The blister 4-pack of AAs the gremlin ate every week, and the screw-down battery door it came off of.

gremlin_fur.notes: Locks of loose fur from the one somebody tried to give a haircut.

gremlin_reboot.notes: The 2010s comeback: same gremlin, LCD eyes that roll, louder fur, worse attitude.

gremlin_sling.notes: The padded cloth carry pouch with a shoulder strap, so it could talk at you hands-free.

gusher_box.notes: The box of liquid-center fruit snacks, one pouch torn open and spilling.

hazelnut_wafer_bar.notes: The two-bar hazelnut wafer, in its white wrapper, or one bar already out of it.

head_unit.notes: The in-dash deck with the detachable face: blue display, a volume knob the size of a cookie, graphics that looked like a energy drink exploded. Face half popped off, ready for the case.

hood_clan.notes: A clan member: a big hooded figure with the extras: mask, shades, chain, backpack, something in hand.

hood_mini.notes: A mini: a small hooded figure, plain, in one of the squad colors.

hooded_figure.notes: The one at the desk: a plain green hoodie, hood up.

hours_mailer.notes: The envelope with the round lump in it: 1000 HOURS FREE in letters bigger than your address. Opened by the dog. Coaster number forty.

hwatu_cards.notes: Flower cards: little thick red-backed cards, twelve months of plants. Played on a blanket after dinner.

im_stickers.notes: A sheet of AIMLESS messenger stickers starring BLIPPY: away message, door opening, door slamming. Half of them already on a binder.

inflatable_chair.notes: A crushed inflatable chair: translucent neon vinyl tubes, the valve, the seams.

instant_camera.notes: The boxy instant camera: a black wedge with a lens like a porthole, a flip-up flash, a sunset stripe down the face and a fresh print sliding out of its mouth.

instant_photos.notes: A loose fan of instant prints: square-ish photo, fat white chin, sharpie caption. Shook them anyway.

jelly_babies.notes: Floury little gummy babies in six colors. Heads first, always.

jersey_scrap.notes: A torn chunk of a replica jersey: mesh weave, name across the shoulders, the big tackle-twill number.

joy_egg.notes: The split plastic egg: in its foil, or opened, cream half and toy half, with the little spoon.

keitai_strap.notes: A clump of phone straps that outlived the phone.

kid_blimp.notes: The toy of the awards-show blimp: orange, splat-logo'd, would not fly no matter how hard you threw it.

kids_choc_bar.notes: The little single bar with the milky middle, wrapped or half-eaten.

kinkeshi.notes: A one-color rubber muscle-man eraser: masked, flexing, and useless for erasing.

kush_ball.notes: The rubber-filament ball: a thousand floppy strands, every one of them dusty.

latefee_receipt.notes: The late fee receipt, curled from the thermal printer: one tape, nine days late, a total that could have bought the movie.

launchables.notes: The build-it-yourself lunch tray: crackers, cheese squares, meat circles, yellow sleeve half off.

lava_lamp_era.notes: The rocket-shaped lava lamp: gold cone base, tapered glass, glowing wax blobs, gold cap.

light_gun.notes: The orange light gun: point it at the screen, shoot the ducks, blame the dog.

light_strand.notes: Old fat C9 bulbs on green wire, the strand nobody could untangle.

loop_track.notes: Orange plastic race track with the loop-de-loop, the blue connector tabs and one car that never made it.

loose_socks.notes: One loose sock, bunched down the shin the way they were meant to be, held up with sock glue.

lunch_tray.notes: The cafeteria compartment tray: rectangle pizza, tater tots, canned corn, a spork, a bad decision.

magic_wand.notes: A toy magical-girl wand of our own: star head, heart jewel, little wings, ribbons. The light-up button stopped.

mascot_plush.notes: Our own tournament mascot, a big-mouthed frog in a jersey with a ball under one arm. Claw-machine quality.

memory_card_stack.notes: A small stack of labeled memory cards, one of them holding a 60-hour save nobody backed up.

menko_card.notes: A round slapping card, thick board, bent from being slammed on the pavement.

micro_cars.notes: A fistful of tiny cars, the kind you lost in the carpet by the dozen.

mini_barrels.notes: Twist-top mini barrels of colored sugar water. The blue one was the currency of the lunch table.

mini_helmet.notes: A mini replica football helmet: glossy shell, center stripe, grey facemask, the logo decal.

mini_pod.notes: The mini: anodized aluminum in five colors, the click wheel printed in the same color as the shell.

modem_56k.notes: The external 56K: a flat box with a row of lights that blinked through the handshake, the scream that came with it, and the one family member who picked up the phone at 98%.

monster_card.notes: A pocket-moanster trading card: yellow border, HP, energy pips, our own critter. Blue back.

monster_cart.notes: The little grey cart, clipped corner, label in red, blue or yellow.

monster_dex.notes: The red flip-open monster encyclopedia toy: big blue lens, three little lights, a screen, a lid.

monster_playset.notes: The black-and-green horned-beast clamshell: the whole head opened into a doom fortress for one tiny guy.

mood_ring.notes: A mood ring: thin silver band, a big oval stone shifting blue-green-purple.

moon_shooz.notes: Mini trampolines strapped to your feet: a plastic tub, a black mat on bungee cords, a sole and two straps.

mousepad.notes: The screensaver mousepad: winged floppy disks flying across a night sky, a parody of the screensaver your dad paid for. The fabric pilled where the mouse lived.

nano_pod.notes: The nano: thinner than a pencil, glossy, a color screen the size of a postage stamp. Scratched by looking at it.

neon_coin.notes: A fat coin in the brand color, a black CCFF00 stamped in the face.

neon_folder.notes: The pocket folder from the book fair: rainbow, glitter dolphins, a unicorn who has seen things.

neon_frame.notes: A square that is only the outline of one. The black shows through.

neon_pig.notes: The piggy bank in the brand colors: gloss black, with a CCFF00 snout, eyes and coin slot that glow.

neon_sign.notes: A small bent-glass neon sign (a heart, a lightning bolt, a cocktail glass) on a black backing grid.

neon_square_big.notes: The headliner: one big flat square that says what it is.

nerd_blaster.notes: The orange-and-blue foam dart blaster and the darts that ended up on the roof.

new_release_case.notes: The NEW RELEASE case: red sash sticker, the guarantee in fine print, out of stock since Tuesday, and the one copy left was behind the counter with a mustache guy's name on it.

opera_carded.notes: A figure still sealed on its cardback. Nobody opened these. Okay, everybody opened these.

opera_figures.notes: Loose figures, one missing its gun, one chewed by a younger brother.

opera_mailaway.notes: The mail-away mystery figure: white box, baggie, eleven weeks of checking the mailbox.

opera_mask.notes: OVERLORD VEX's helm, the drugstore costume version: crimson, gold ram horns, a crest and a slit visor.

opera_saber.notes: The collapsible toy laser sword: two blade sections out, the third jammed forever.

opera_ship.notes: THE RUSTY COMET: our freighter. Swept wedge hull, twin engines, bubble cockpit, a dorsal fin.

opera_vhs.notes: The boxed trilogy: three tapes in a slipcase, 'digitally remastered', for the second time this decade.

orange_jug.notes: The orange 'drink' jug every mom thought was juice. It was not juice.

orange_vhs.notes: An orange clamshell kids' VHS of a cartoon taped off a cable channel that was mostly slime.

orb_bottle.notes: The 1997 drink with gel balls floating in it like a lava lamp you were supposed to drink.

os_box.notes: Boxed OS software: a fat cardboard box of floppies or one CD, clouds on the front, a window cracked clean through the middle of the logo. Start me up.

p2p_sleeve.notes: A paper CD sleeve from the song-sharing years, its sticker from the app that got the whole dorm's internet cut off: a sour lime in headphones, or a cat asleep on the download button.

party_cup.notes: The red party cup, crushed flat on one side like they all were by the end.

pda.notes: The stylus organizer: a green-grey screen you wrote on in a made-up alphabet, four round app buttons, and a stylus that was lost by Tuesday.

persimmon.notes: A squat orange persimmon with its four-leaf cap. Sometimes a dried one, wrinkled and frosted.

phone_cord.notes: Twenty-five feet of beige phone line, from the kitchen jack to the computer in the den, clear plastic plug on each end with the little clip already snapped off.

pick_bag.notes: The striped paper bag, top twisted shut, corners gone see-through from the sugar.

piggy_bank.notes: Fat body, big snout, real ears, a curly tail and a coin slot. Five breeds: pink ceramic, gold, a tusked iron boar, plush, and chrome.

pilgrim_hat.notes: The construction-paper pilgrim hat from second grade.

pixel_frame.notes: A framed picture off the wall: black frame, a pixel-art square inside (the frames a room hangs its NFTs in).

pixel_hoodie.notes: A hoodie laid flat, arms out, built from square steps so it reads as pixels.

pizza_box.notes: The personal pan pizza you earned by reading, with the star button you wore to prove it.

plasma_ball.notes: A plasma ball: clear globe on a black base, a glowing core, purple lightning filaments to the glass.

plastic_lunchbox.notes: The molded plastic one that replaced the tin: fat rounded corners, two-tone, a raised sticker panel.

pocket_diecast.notes: A palm-sized die-cast car with opening-nothing and suspension that actually bounces. Sometimes still in its box.

pocket_handheld.notes: The vertical pocket color handheld in see-through grape (or teal, lime, berry, clear).

pocket_playset.notes: The pink pocket compact that opened into a tiny house, with a peg doll you lost within the hour.

pog_slammer.notes: The heavy metal slammer: a thick disc with a raised rim and a stamped design.

pog_tube.notes: A clear tube of pogs, colored caps, the top pog showing its art.

popcorn_bag.notes: Microwave popcorn, puffed and steaming, a butter stain through the THIS SIDE UP. Somebody pushed the POPCORN button and walked away.

puff_bag.notes: Cheese puffs: the orange bag, the orange dust, the orange fingers.

pumpkin_pail.notes: The plastic jack-o'-lantern candy bucket, black handle and all.

purikura_sheet.notes: A sheet of photo-booth stickers, half of them already peeled off and stuck in somebody's notebook.

putty_egg.notes: The plastic egg of noise putty. Push your finger in. Act surprised. Get sent to the hall.

razor_phone.notes: The razor-thin metal flip phone: etched keypad that glowed blue, the chin at the bottom, and the hinge that cracked open with one flick of the wrist.

rca_cables.notes: Twisted-pair RCA interconnects, blue jacket, chunky gold plugs with a red ring and a white ring. Paid extra for the gold. Heard the difference. Didn't.

rental_card.notes: The membership card: blue plastic, the cracked brick, a barcode, a signature strip signed in gel pen. The most valuable ID a fourteen-year-old owned.

rental_game.notes: The game rental case: a smaller clamshell, a grey cartridge with a rental sticker over the art, and the save file of a stranger who was already on the last level.

rental_vhs.notes: The rental clamshell: blue plastic, a yellow BLOCKBUSTED cover, the barcode, the category sticker, and a tape that was not rewound.

rf_switch.notes: The RF switch box: TV / GAME slider, coax tail, two spade lugs for the screws on the back of the set.

ring_candy.notes: The giant-jewel candy ring. Worn for status, licked in public, sticky until Thursday.

ripcord_launcher.notes: The launcher: a toothed rip-cord half pulled out, the T-handle on the end.

robo_car.notes: The robot-that-is-also-a-car: hood for a chest, wheels on the shins, a spoiler for wings. Ours, not theirs.

satin_jacket.notes: A shredded chunk of the shiny team jacket everybody's cousin had: satin shell, striped knit collar, snaps.

scented_markers.notes: Fat scented markers with fruit-colored caps; one cap is always missing and that one is dried out.

school_milk.notes: The half-pint chocolate milk carton, opened wrong, spout torn into a ragged mouth.

seal_sticker.notes: The holographic sticker out of a 30-yen wafer. Kids bought the wafers and threw the wafers away.

shiny_badge.notes: The shiny: a foil team crest. Worth five normal ones on the playground exchange rate.

sidekick_phone.notes: The swivel-screen texter: the screen flipped around to reveal a full keyboard, a trackball, and the first time you could AIM from the back of algebra.

signed_baseball.notes: An autographed ball on its little stand. The signature is real. The person is not famous.

skin_printout.notes: An inkjet printout of a media-player skin somebody was proud of: the spectrum bars, the scrolling title, the slogan about whipping a farm animal. Banding from the cyan cartridge running low.

skull_candle.notes: A skull-shaped candle, face toward -Y: cranium, brow, two deep sockets, a nose hole, a row of teeth.

slim_tower_console.notes: The black monolith, standing up: half its side ribbed in parallel grooves, a tray seam, a blue badge.

slime_cereal.notes: A cartoon tie-in cereal box: neon O's, slime marshmallows, a toy that broke on the drive home.

slime_tub.notes: The tub of official green slime, lid off, slime making a break for it.

snake_phone.notes: The brick that never died: blue-grey shell, one big navi key, a green screen with Snake on it. Dropped down the stairs, battery flew out, put it back in, still worked.

snapback_cap.notes: A two-tone snapback with a flat brim and the gold sticker nobody ever peeled off.

soggy_blaster.notes: The neon pump water blaster: tank on top, pump slide underneath, an orange nozzle, a lawsuit-level range.

songpyeon.notes: Half-moon rice cakes in pastel colors, pinched shut over sesame or bean, steamed on pine needles.

sour_pack.notes: The face-melting sour candy bag, a few twist-wrapped pieces loose. Held in mouth for 30 seconds on a dare.

spam_can.notes: The canned ham with the pull-ring lid. In Seoul it comes in a gift box and nobody laughs.

spam_gift_box.notes: The holiday gift set: a blue box, a plastic carry handle, cans in a molded tray. Given to bosses.

speaker_6x9.notes: The 6x9 oval for the rear deck: stamped basket, a cone in mica glitter or blue poly, a little tweeter on a bridge across the middle, and a sticker promising more watts than the car had.

splat_sign.notes: The orange splat logo sign off the studio wall. Our splat, our letters, our lawsuit-free goo.

splurge_can.notes: The lime-green citrus soda of 1997: neon can, red letters, the energy drink before energy drinks.

squeeze_buddy.notes: A character-shaped squeeze drink: twist off his head, squeeze his guts out. That's lunch.

stereo_viewer.notes: The red stereo picture viewer and a reel of 3D photos of somewhere you never went.

stick_biscuit_box.notes: The chocolate-dipped biscuit sticks, red box, one end torn open with a few sticks sliding out.

sticker_album.notes: The album, cover curling open on a page that is about half full. It was always about half full.

sticker_packet.notes: A five-sticker packet, sealed or torn across the top with the stickers half out.

stiff_cap.notes: The stiffening capacitor: a chrome can the size of a soda bottle with a blue digital readout on top that dipped from 14.4 to 11.9 every time the bass hit. That was the point.

strategy_guide.notes: The official strategy guide: every secret, every map, a poster stapled in the middle.

stretch_man.notes: The gel-filled muscle man: one arm pulled to twice its length, slowly not coming back.

subwoofer.notes: The 10 or the 12: a fat rubber surround you could pinch, a cone that hopped a quarter inch on every kick drum, a magnet stack heavier than the spare tire. Rattled the license plate off.

surprise_egg.notes: The foil egg, or what is left once it was opened: two chocolate halves, white inside, and the capsule.

surprise_slip.notes: The accordion-folded instruction slip, the part everyone threw away first.

surprise_toy.notes: The toy: a painted little critter, a four-piece buggy, or the parts still on the sprue.

swap_stack.notes: The swaps: a fat stack of doubles held with a rubber band, thumbed until the corners went round.

swirl_console.notes: The white rounded box with the orange pinwheel on its lid: dead too soon.

tango_football.notes: A match ball with the twelve-circle triad pattern, scuffed grey from the street. Sometimes half flat.

tazo.notes: One disc out of a chip bag. Some were shiny. You traded three for a shiny.

tazo_board.notes: The cardboard collector board with a round hole for every disc. It was never full.

tazo_chip_bag.notes: The bag you bought for the disc inside. The chips were a bonus.

tazo_tube.notes: The clear collector tube with the colored cap, packed with discs, rattling in a backpack.

team_scarf.notes: A knitted bar scarf, folded three times, the team chant spelled down its length. Tassels on both ends.

theater_candy.notes: Theater-box candy from the rack by the register: a long cardboard box, flap torn open, a few pieces rattling loose. Overpriced. Bought anyway.

ticker_tape.notes: A long strip of tape, coiled like it fell off the machine, with a loose end.

tickle_monster.notes: Red plush cyclops with a laugh box in its gut. Squeeze, it giggles. Squeeze at 2am, it giggles anyway.

tie_dye_shirt.notes: A wadded tie-dye T-shirt, the spiral of the dye still showing.

tin_lunchbox.notes: The embossed metal lunch box with a Saturday-morning cartoon on it, and its matching plastic thermos.

toy_oven.notes: The light-bulb oven: purple and pink, two fake burners, one real burn.

trapped_keeper.notes: The zip-around trapper binder: loud cover, chunky side zipper, the velcro flap that ripped in class.

trial_cd.notes: The free trial disc. Arrived in the mail, in the cereal box, in the bag at the store, under the windshield wiper. Coaster count at its peak: one per household per day.

trial_tin.notes: The fancy one: the trial disc in a little metal tin, lid printed in silver and blue, hinged open with the disc winking inside. Too nice to throw out. Too useless to keep.

trident_controller.notes: Three handles, one stick dead center, a blue A, a green B and four yellow arrows.

trip_it.notes: The ankle-hop toy: a hoop for your ankle, a long stem, a ball at the end and a lap counter.

troll_doll.notes: A pencil-topper troll: chubby vinyl body, wide grin, a tall shock of neon hair.

tweeter.notes: A component tweeter on its swivel cup: a little silk dome, a chrome ring, a stick-on base you glued to the dash and aimed at your own ear.

twin_grip_controller.notes: Grey, two long grips, two sticks low in the middle, four face buttons in a diamond.

umaibo.notes: The ten-yen corn puff stick, in a printed wrapper, or bitten open with the hollow puff showing.

underglow.notes: A neon underglow tube: glass-clear tube, gas glowing inside, black end caps and a cord to the switch on the dash. Made a Civic look like it was hovering. Got pulled over for it.

vmu_controller.notes: White, rounded, a memory card with its own little screen jammed in the top, cord out the bottom.

vuvuzela.notes: The bell half of a two-piece plastic stadium horn. One B-flat, ninety minutes, the whole summer of 2010.

wallchart.notes: The free newspaper wallchart, folded in half, groups filled in in pen until your team went out.

wax_pack.notes: A torn wax pack of cards: crimped wax wrapper, a pink slab of gum that could cut glass, two cards out.

white_mice.notes: Chalky sugar mice, white and pink, with a sugar-string tail.

wide_handheld.notes: The landscape handheld: indigo, flared ends, two shoulder buttons.

wonder_ball.notes: The foil chocolate ball with the surprise inside. The surprise was always a smaller disappointment.

wrestler_fig.notes: A rubbery wrestling figure in neon tights with a gold title belt the size of his torso.

y2k_glasses.notes: The 2000 glasses: the two zeros in the middle are the lenses.

yak_toy.notes: The handheld voice recorder toy: a fat translucent pill with one huge thumb button. Six seconds of memory, all of it fart noises.

yapper_boy.notes: The movie-kid tape recorder: a silver brick with a carry handle bigger than the kid's hand and a mic on a stalk that pulls out the side. Slows your voice down. Prank calls the hotel.

yut_sticks.notes: Four half-round sticks for yut nori, the flat faces up or down; one has the X that sends you back.
